title: Step diagnostics in policy.rego use entry.location, not job id or step name
answers: policy error message says wrong job or step for unnamed step
how do policy messages identify a step
which location format do policy denials use
body:
Symptom: a policy denial names a job but not which step, or prints an empty step name for unnamed steps.
Root cause: messages formerly used job_id and step.name, which are missing for unnamed steps and do not identify parallel children.
Fix pattern: step_entries(inp) attaches a `location` string such as "job 'X', step #N" or "job 'X', step #N, parallel step #M"; messages format it with %s, e.g. "actions/github-script at %s must have 'retries' set".
Constraints: keep the "at %s" phrasing consistent across step rules so the output is uniform; the composite-action branch of step_entries is the source of its location format, so reuse entry.location rather than building one per rule.
applies: Writing or editing deny messages for step-level rules in .github/policy.rego.
says: Workflow policy error messages do not indicate which step caused the failure.
The pipeline policy check displays a blank step name when steps are unnamed.
Policy violation warnings should clearly identify the exact job and step number.
Policy failure reports do not specify which parallel step failed the validation check.
Make workflow compliance error messages consistently show the exact location of failing steps.
search: Step-level denial messages in .github/policy.rego must use entry.location from step_entries(inp) rather than job_id or step.name. Formatting messages with %s and entry.location (such as "job 'X', step #N") correctly identifies parallel children and unnamed steps that lack a step name. Rules must reuse entry.location and consistently use the "at %s" phrasing to keep step diagnostics uniform.
